cards.name: Graphic Equalizer (10 Bands)
cards.summary: Fixed-frequency equalizer with 10 octave-spaced sliders (about 31 Hz to 16 kHz) that boost or cut each band. Fast broad tone shaping without choosing frequencies.
use_for: Cut rumble below ~63 Hz on location VO and interview audio
Tame 250 Hz mud on phone-recorded or small-room VO
Dip the 1-4 kHz bands of a music bed so the VO sits on top
Rough tone match between two interview mics in a documentary
avoid: Big boosts (above ~0.6) sound harsh and clip; cut rather than boost
Too coarse for hum, whistles or single tones: use Parametric Equalizer, Notch Filter or DeHummer
Never set Reset or Is Processing (internal button and status flag)

params.name: EQ Band 1
params.typical: 0.5 = flat; 0.35-0.45 to cut rumble under VO

measured.figure: band of the largest boost (Hz, third-octave resolution)

params.name: EQ Band 2
params.typical: 0.4-0.47 on VO; 0.52-0.56 for heavier trailer music

measured.figure: band of the largest boost (Hz, third-octave resolution)
band of the deepest cut (Hz, third-octave resolution)

params.name: EQ Band 8
params.typical: 0.52-0.55 for clearer VO; 0.45-0.48 on a music bed under VO

measured.figure: band of the largest boost (Hz, third-octave resolution)

params.name: Gain
params.typical: 0.5 = 0 dB; lower slightly if boosts push peaks

params.name: Range
params.does: dB span of every band slider
params.typical: leave default 0.3924 = 48 dB (Audition's documented 1.5-120 dB Range, dB = 1.5 + 118.5*v; the default decodes to exactly 48.0)

measured.figure: band of the largest boost (Hz, third-octave resolution)

cards.scripting: Every value is normalized 0-1 (Effect Controls shows dB). EQ Band n centre ~31.25 Hz x 2^(n-1): 31, 63, 125, 250, 500, 1k, 2k, 4k, 8k, 16k. 0.5 = 0 dB on every band and on Gain (from defaults). The slider span follows Range: the default 0.3924 decodes exactly to 48 dB on Audition's 1.5-120 dB scale, so each band spans about +/-24 dB (measured: +22-24 dB at 1) and 0.01 = ~0.48 dB. Set Range before the bands. Never set Reset (momentary button that flattens all bands) or Is Processing (status flag). Accuracy: leave default (higher = better low-band precision, more CPU). Ignore the unnamed bool row. demo_settings is a cuts-only 'telephone' curve, so it cannot clip. Apply with qeClip.addAudioEffect(qe.project.getAudioEffectByName(name)); the new component is the clip's last component. Measured: bands 1 / 4 / 7 / 10 boost the lowest / 250 Hz / 2 kHz / 16 kHz bands by 22-24 dB at 1, band 4 at 0 cuts 250 Hz by 17 dB: octave bands 31.25 x 2^(n-1) Hz confirmed (band 1 reads at the analysis floor), each about +/-24 dB at the default Range.

cards.name: GuitarSuite
cards.summary: Guitar amp chain (from Audition): compressor, filter, distortion and speaker-cabinet modeler with a dry/wet Mix. Made for guitar, but roughens any sound.
use_for: Crunchy amp tone on a guitar music bed for a trailer or sports reel
Gritty megaphone / rally-loudspeaker voice in a satire reel (with Bandpass)
Dirty, aggressive impact or riser SFX for trailer hits
Broken-speaker lo-fi treatment on a quoted clip
avoid: On documentary VO or interviews: wrecks intelligibility
Defaults are already heavily distorted (Dist Amount 0.72, Mix 1): lower Mix or Dist Amount first
Distortion raises level and harshness: follow with Hard Limiter

params.name: Dist Amount
params.does: Distortion drive. Measured on a 1 kHz tone: THD 0.006 % at 0, 94 % at the default 0.722, 105 % at 1; at its defaults the tone rises 7.6 dB.
params.typical: 0.1-0.3 for grit you can still read words through; the default 0.722 is already fuzz

measured.figure: total harmonic distortion (%)

params.name: Mix
params.does: Dry/wet balance of the whole chain
params.typical: 1 = fully processed (default); 0.3-0.5 keeps a voice readable

params.name: Box Model
params.typical: leave default 0.2857 (2/7: index 2 of 8 options if there are 8; option count not verified)

params.name: Dist Type
params.typical: default 0.5 (middle of an odd option count; labels unverified)

params.name: Bypass Filter
params.does: Switches the filter stage off (1) or on (0)
params.typical: default 1; set 0 to use Filter Freq / Filter Resonance

params.name: Filter Freq
params.typical: default 0.049 = 1 kHz if linear 20 Hz-20 kHz (inferred)

params.name: Bypass Distortion
params.does: Switches the distortion stage off (1) or on (0)

cards.scripting: All values normalized 0-1. Dropdowns (Dist Type, Filter Type, Filter, Box Model) are normalized too: option i of n is i/(n-1) (Box Model default 0.2857 = 2/7, consistent with 8 cabinets but also 15; Dist Type 0.5 only tells us the count is odd). Option counts and labels are not verified, so pick by ear or read the panel. Bypass rows are 0/1 switches. Filter Freq looks linear 20-20000 Hz (Hz = 20 + v*19980; the default 0.049049 decodes to exactly 1000 Hz). 'Filter' vs 'Filter Type' meaning is unclear; leave both at default unless verified. No AE equivalent. Ignore the unnamed bool row.

cards.name: Hard Limiter
cards.summary: Brick-wall limiter: keeps audio from going above a set ceiling and can push the input into that ceiling to make it louder. The usual last effect on a mix.
use_for: Final ceiling so reel and YouTube exports never clip (about -1 dBTP)
Catch shouts, claps and mic bumps in rally or interview audio
Add 2-4 dB of loudness to a VO + music mix for social reels
Safety on trailer impact hits and risers
avoid: Heavy Input Boost pumps and flattens music: keep gain reduction to a few dB
Not a loudness normaliser: measure LUFS separately (Loudness Meter, or export Loudness Normalization)
Does nothing on quiet material whose peaks never reach the ceiling

params.name: Maximum Amplitude
params.does: Output ceiling. Measured on a -6 dBFS tone: the output peak sat at -76 / -50 / -25 / -6 dBFS for 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 0.999, i.e. ceiling dBFS = 100 v - 100 (confirmed).
params.typical: 0.99 = about -1 dB (scale looks linear -100..0 dB: default 0.999 = -0.1 dB); 0.98 = -2 dB for strict social delivery

measured.figure: output peak change (dB)

params.name: Input Boost
params.does: Gain into the limiter (louder, more limiting). Measured on a -18 dBFS tone: 0.5 = -25 dB, 0.6667 = 0 dB, 0.8333 = +17.9 dB, already at the ceiling (about 150 dB per unit, dB = 150 v - 100, until the limiter holds it).
params.typical: 0.6667 = 0 dB (default); 0.7 = +5 dB, 0.733 = +10 dB into the ceiling

measured.figure: level change (dB)

params.name: Limit True Peak
params.does: Limits inter-sample (true) peaks, not just sample peaks

params.name: Release Time
params.does: How fast gain recovers after a peak
params.typical: default 0.375 (100 ms in Audition-derived scale); leave for VO

params.name: Look-Ahead Time
params.does: How early the limiter reacts to an incoming peak

params.name: Link Channels
params.does: Same gain reduction on L and R

cards.scripting: All values normalized 0-1; Effect Controls shows dB/ms. Maximum Amplitude is -100..0 dB linear (measured: 0.5 = -50 dBFS); Input Boost is about 150 dB per unit around 0.6667 = 0 dB (measured: 0.5 = -25 dB). 'Decay to Ceiling' is a 0/1 switch of unclear effect: leave at default 1. For a whole-mix limit the usual place is the Mix track in the Audio Track Mixer, which documented ExtendScript does not expose: apply it to a nested sequence's clip instead, or use export Loudness Normalization with a true-peak limit. Ignore the unnamed bool row. No AE equivalent.

measured.how: Premiere 26 render, 3 s test signal per setting, analysed with ffmpeg (live wave 3, 2026-10-14)

cards.name: Loudness Meter
cards.summary: Meters loudness (momentary, short-term and integrated LUFS plus true peak) against a target level. Analysis only: it does not change the sound.
use_for: Check a reel mix lands near -14 LUFS integrated for Instagram / YouTube
Check broadcast deliverables at -23 / -24 LUFS
Spot VO passages that sit far below the music bed
Confirm true peak stays under -1 dBTP before export
avoid: It changes nothing: never rely on it to fix levels
A script cannot read its readings: in the pipeline measure with ffmpeg ebur128 / loudnorm instead
On a single clip it measures only that clip, not the mix

params.name: Target Level
params.does: Target loudness the meter compares against. Measured: no change to the audio at 0 or 1 (a meter only); the LUFS value of a setting cannot be read from the render.
params.typical: default 0.433, probably -23 LUFS on a -36..-6 scale (then -14 LUFS = 0.733); unverified

measured.figure: level change (dB)

params.name: Reset on Playback
params.does: Restart the integrated reading each time playback starts
params.typical: 1 when checking a whole mix pass

cards.scripting: Only useful to a human watching the effect panel; it makes no audible change and exposes no readable measurement to ExtendScript, so an automated pipeline should skip it and measure the rendered file (ffmpeg ebur128 / loudnorm, or export Loudness Normalization). For a whole-mix reading it belongs on the Mix track (Audio Track Mixer), which documented ExtendScript does not expose. Target Level and Maximum True Peak mappings are inferred from defaults only (a render cannot show them: measured, Target Level 0 and 1 leave the audio unchanged). Scale and Unit are normalized dropdowns with unverified labels. Ignore the unnamed bool row.

cards.name: Mastering
cards.summary: All-in-one mastering chain (from Audition): 3-band EQ (low shelf, peak, high shelf), reverb, exciter, stereo widener and loudness maximizer with output gain.
use_for: Quick polish and loudness for a music bed or trailer score
Brighten a dull stock music track
Widen a stereo music bed so the centred VO has room
One-effect final sweetening on a short social reel's music
avoid: Defaults are NOT neutral (reverb 0.1, exciter 0.8, maximizer 0.2, EQ moves): set every control deliberately

params.typical: 0.2-0.4 for music beds (about -19 to -16 LUFS from a -21 LUFS source)

measured.figure: integrated loudness (LUFS)

params.name: EQ Band 3 Gain
params.typical: 0.667 = 0 dB (inferred); default 0.709 is a small boost

params.name: Output Gain
params.does: Final output level. Measured: 0.3333 = -12.5 dB, 0.6667 = +2.5 dB, 1 = +17.5 dB: dB = 45 v - 27.5, so 0 dB is 0.611 and the default 0.6667 already adds 2.5 dB.

cards.name: Balance
cards.summary: Shifts a stereo clip's level between the left and right channels. Works only on stereo clips; on a mono clip it cannot be applied.
use_for: Fix camera or interview audio that is louder on one channel
Place a phone-call or radio voice slightly to one side in a two-voice bit
Nudge a stereo music bed off-centre under a centred VO
avoid: Mono clips: the effect does not attach (it failed silently in the harvest)
For dual-mono interviews where one channel is a second mic, use Fill Left with Right / Fill Right with Left or Modify > Audio Channels instead

params.name: Balance
params.does: Left / right balance. Measured on a split stereo pair: 0 = full left (right channel silent), 0.5 = centre (unchanged), 1 = full right (left channel silent).

measured.figure: left channel level (dBFS rms)
measured.signal: a split stereo pair (L 440 Hz at -12 dBFS, R 1 kHz at -24 dBFS)

cards.scripting: Stereo clips only (on a mono clip it does not attach: the mono harvest read the clip Volume row; the batch now holds the stereo dump, match 'Internal Audio Balance'). One property, 'Balance', normalized: 0 = full left (the right channel is silenced), 0.5 = centre (default, unchanged), 1 = full right (measured on a split stereo pair, live wave 3). It attenuates one side; it does not move one channel's sound into the other (use Channel Mixer or Fill Left/Right for that). Check that the last component's displayName is 'Balance' after adding it.

cards.name: Bandpass
cards.summary: Keeps a band of frequencies around a centre frequency and removes everything above and below it; Q sets how narrow the band is.
use_for: Phone-call or walkie-talkie voice for a quoted call or leaked audio in a news reel
Old-radio / archival broadcast feel on historical documentary clips
Muffled 'other room' or flashback voice in a trailer
Megaphone rally voice in a satire reel (with GuitarSuite)
avoid: On the main VO: sounds cheap and thin
Very high Q gives a whistling, ringing tone

params.name: Cutoff
params.does: Centre frequency of the kept band (called 'Center' in Adobe docs). Measured: the kept band centre is about 24 000 x v^2 Hz (0.1 = 250 Hz, 0.25 = 1.6 kHz, 0.5 = 6.3 kHz, 0.75 = 12.7 kHz, third-octave readings): v = sqrt(Hz / 24 000).

measured.figure: band of the largest boost (Hz, third-octave resolution)

params.name: Q
params.does: Band width: low = wide band, high = narrow band

cards.scripting: Values normalized 0-1; the Cutoff-to-Hz curve is measured: about 24 000 x v^2 Hz (see Cutoff). Any setting is clearly audible (everything outside the band is removed). In AE, two High-Low Pass instances (one high pass, one low pass) give the same result. The recipe widens the band over 1 s for a 'phone call opens up to full voice' reveal; whether Q 0 sounds fully open is unverified, so cross-fade to an unfiltered copy if it does not. Ignore the unnamed bool row.

cards.name: Simple Notch Filter
cards.summary: Removes a narrow band around one frequency and leaves the rest untouched. Used to kill a single steady tone such as hum or a whine.
use_for: Remove 50 Hz mains hum (India) from location or interview audio
Cut a constant whine from a projector, AC unit or camera fan
Remove a single feedback ring in rally or press-conference audio
avoid: Hum has harmonics (100, 150, 200 Hz): one notch rarely clears it, use DeHummer (50 Hz) or Notch Filter with several bands
A wide (low Q) notch thins the voice

params.name: Cutoff
params.does: Frequency to remove (called 'Center' in Adobe docs). Measured: the notch sits at about 24 000 x v^2 Hz (0.1 = 250 Hz, 0.25 = 1.6 kHz, 0.5 = 6.3 kHz, 0.75 = 12.7 kHz), 5.8-9.2 dB deep on pink noise at the default Q: v = sqrt(Hz / 24 000).

measured.figure: band of the deepest cut (Hz, third-octave resolution)

params.name: Q
params.does: Notch width: higher = narrower (standard filter convention; direction not verified for this Premiere-internal filter)
params.typical: 0.7-1 for a surgical cut (default 0.5); if the voice thins audibly, the direction is reversed

cards.scripting: Values normalized 0-1; the Cutoff-to-Hz curve is measured: about 24 000 x v^2 Hz, the same as Bandpass (see Cutoff). The Q direction is also unread: confirm once by ear (a narrow notch on a VO is nearly inaudible, a wide one thins it). Inaudible on clean audio by design, so no demo settings. For hum, DeHummer with 50 Hz is the safer automatic choice. Ignore the unnamed bool row.

cards.name: Bass
cards.summary: Boosts or cuts the low frequencies (roughly 200 Hz and below) with a single Boost control.
use_for: Add weight to trailer hits, booms and cinematic music
Slight warmth on a thin phone-recorded VO
Cut boom from a music bed so the VO stays clear
Deep 'announcer' feel on a promo title VO

params.name: Boost
params.does: Low-frequency gain. Measured at 63 Hz on pink noise: 0 = -23.2 dB, 0.25 = -12.3, 0.75 = +12.9, 1 = +26.0 dB (1 kHz moves under 1.6 dB): about 49 dB per unit around 0.5, the +/-24 dB span confirmed.

cards.name: Delay
cards.summary: Single echo with feedback: replays the sound after a set time, repeating and fading according to Feedback.
use_for: Echo-out on the last word of a trailer or teaser line
Dramatic repeat on a key quote in a political or news reel
Slapback on whooshes and impact SFX
PA / stadium feel on a rally speech snippet
avoid: On continuous VO: smears words and hurts intelligibility
The echo stops at the clip end: extend the clip (or nest with silence after) so the tail is not cut
Feedback above ~0.7 builds into long runaway repeats

params.name: Delay
params.does: Echo time. Measured: the echo comes 2 x value seconds after the sound (0.1 = 0.2 s, 0.3 = 0.6 s, 0.6 = 1.2 s): 0..1 = 0..2 s confirmed.
params.typical: 0..1 = 0..2 s (2 s max per Adobe docs; default 0.5 = 1 s). 0.1-0.25 (0.2-0.5 s) dramatic echo; 0.03-0.06 slapback

measured.figure: first echo after the click (s)

params.name: Feedback
params.does: Amount fed back = number of repeats

cards.scripting: Values normalized 0-1; Delay time mapping (linear 0-2 s) measured: 0.1 = 0.2 s, 0.6 = 1.2 s. For an echo-out, either razor the last word into its own clip and apply Delay there with room after it, or keyframe Mix as in the recipe (seconds from clip start; the 2.0 s point is an example for where the last word lands). Ignore the unnamed bool row.

cards.name: Highpass
cards.summary: Removes everything below a cutoff frequency and passes the highs. The standard rumble, wind and handling-noise cleanup for voice.

params.name: Cutoff
params.does: Frequency below which audio is removed. Measured on pink noise: -3 dB at 92 Hz / 1.9 kHz / 7.3 kHz / 15.1 kHz for 0.05 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75, close to Hz = 26 500 x v^1.9 (within about 6 %): neither linear nor logarithmic.

measured.figure: -3 dB cut-off (Hz)
